sources.zh: 台積電 2024 年 4 月 24 日發表 A16 製程，預計 2026 年生產

sources.en: DNA is about 22–26 angstroms (2.2–2.6 nm) wide
Silicon: single-bond covalent radius 117.6 pm (so neighboring atoms are about 0.235 nm apart); lattice constant 0.5431 nm
sources.zh: 矽：單鍵共價半徑 117.6 皮米（相鄰原子相隔約 0.235 奈米）；晶格常數 0.5431 奈米

sources.en: Fingernails grow about 3.5 mm a month on average (Yaemsiri and others, 2010)
sources.zh: 指甲平均每月約長 3.5 公釐（Yaemsiri 等，2010）

sources.en: A4 paper is 210 × 297 mm
sources.zh: A4 紙的尺寸是 210 × 297 公釐

sources.en: Optical microscopes are limited to about 200 nm by the diffraction of visible light
sources.zh: 光學顯微鏡受可見光繞射限制，解析度約 200 奈米

units.blurb_en: Why chips are stacked together, why AI needs fast memory, and how Taiwan became a chip island.
units.blurb_zh: 晶片為什麼要疊在一起、AI 為什麼需要快速的記憶體，以及台灣怎麼成為晶片島。

lessons.title: Why Do We Stack Chips Together?
lessons.title_zh: 先進封裝：為什麼要把晶片疊在一起？
lessons.blurb_en: One chip cannot be made as big as we like, so engineers put many chips into one package, side by side or stacked like floors in a building. In 3D, compare chips set apart on a board, side by side on an interposer, and stacked, then take the package apart layer by layer.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一顆晶片沒辦法想做多大就做多大，所以工程師把很多顆晶片放進同一個封裝裡：並排，或像大樓的樓層一樣疊起來。在 3D 裡比較三種放法——分開焊在板子上、並排放在中介層上、疊起來——再把封裝一層一層拆開來看。
lessons.big_idea_en: A chip needs a package to protect it and to connect it to the outside. Advanced packaging goes further: it puts several chips into one package, side by side or stacked, and joins them with very short wires. Shorter paths mean data moves faster and uses less power, like turning scattered houses into one tall building.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 晶片需要封裝來保護它，並把它和外面接起來。先進封裝更進一步：把好幾顆晶片放進同一個封裝，並排或疊起來，用很短的線連在一起。路短了，資料就跑得更快、更省電，就像把分散的房子蓋成一棟大樓。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose Apart, Side by side, or Stacked at the top left, and watch the yellow dots of data travel from the blue logic chip to the purple memory chips. Then drag “Take it apart” to pull the layers away from one another and see what a package is made of.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。在左上角選「分開放」「並排」或「疊起來」，看黃色的資料小點從藍色的運算晶片跑到紫色的記憶體晶片。再拉「拆開來看」，把每一層上下拉開，看看一個封裝是用什麼做成的。

board.en: Each chip sits in its own package, and the packages are soldered to a circuit board a few centimeters apart. Data has to leave one package, cross the board, and enter another. For a chip, that is a very long trip.
board.zh: 每顆晶片各有自己的封裝，分開焊在電路板上，彼此相隔幾公分。資料要先離開一個封裝、穿過板子、再進到另一個封裝。對晶片來說，這是很遠的路。

side.en: Now the bare chips sit side by side on one thin slice of silicon called an interposer. Its wires are far finer than the ones on a circuit board, so the chips can sit very close together. This is called 2.5D packaging.
side.zh: 現在把沒有外殼的晶片並排放在同一片薄薄的矽上，這片矽叫做中介層。它上面的線比電路板上的細得多，所以晶片可以靠得非常近。這種做法叫做 2.5D 封裝。

stack.en: Here the memory chips are stacked like floors in a building. Tiny copper posts called TSVs run straight up through the chips like elevators. The data only has to go up a few floors. This is 3D packaging.
stack.zh: 這裡把記憶體晶片像大樓的樓層一樣疊起來。很細的銅柱（矽穿孔，TSV）直直穿過晶片，像電梯一樣。資料只要往上走幾層樓就到了。這就是 3D 封裝。

legend.en: Blue: the logic chip, which does the calculating
legend.zh: 藍色：運算晶片，負責計算

legend.en: Purple: memory chips, which hold the data
legend.zh: 紫色：記憶體晶片，負責放資料

legend.en: Gray-blue: the interposer, a slice of silicon with very fine wires
legend.zh: 灰藍色：中介層，一片佈滿細線的矽

legend.en: Green: the package substrate and the circuit board
legend.zh: 綠色：封裝的基板和電路板

legend.en: Yellow dots: data on its way
legend.zh: 黃色小點：正在路上的資料

lab.scale_en: A teaching diagram, not to scale. The distances (about 3 centimeters, 3 millimeters, and 0.4 millimeters) are example numbers chosen to show the pattern; real products differ. Real packages have thousands of connections where this model shows a few dozen, and real chips are much thinner than they are drawn here.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意圖，不是真實比例。距離（大約 3 公分、3 公釐、0.4 公釐）是為了呈現趨勢所舉的例子，真的產品各有不同。真的封裝有成千上萬個接點，這裡只畫了幾十個；真的晶片也比圖上薄得多。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The three layouts follow Wikipedia, “2.5D integrated circuit” and “Three-dimensional integrated circuit”. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；三種放法依維基百科「2.5D integrated circuit」與「Three-dimensional integrated circuit」條目。

paras: Look inside a phone or a computer and you will see small black squares on a green board. Those squares are not the chips themselves. Each one is a package: a tough case with a chip inside. The package protects the thin silicon from bumps, dust, and damp. It also connects the chip's tiny contacts to the much bigger world of the circuit board.

For a long time, that was the whole job. One chip went into one package, and the packages were soldered onto a board a few centimeters apart. But chips kept getting faster, and the trip between them began to matter. Data from the logic chip, which does the thinking, had to cross the board to reach the memory chip, which holds the data. Every trip took time and energy.

Why not just make one giant chip with everything on it? Because chips cannot grow without limit. The machine that prints the circuits can only expose an area of about 26 by 33 millimeters at a time. Bigger chips also mean fewer chips on each wafer, and one speck of dust can ruin a bigger piece. So engineers took a different road: keep the chips small, and bring them very close together.

The first way is to place bare chips side by side on a thin slice of silicon called an interposer. Its wires are far finer than the wires on a circuit board, so the chips can sit almost touching. This is called 2.5D packaging. Designers can mix and match small chips, called chiplets, a little like building with LEGO bricks.

The second way is to stack chips on top of one another, like floors in a building. Tiny copper posts called through-silicon vias, or TSVs, run straight through the chips like elevators. Now the data travels up a few floors instead of across a city. Shorter wires mean faster signals and less wasted power. But a stack traps heat, so engineers must plan carefully how to keep it cool.

After packaging, every chip is tested before it leaves the factory. Packaging and testing together are a big industry in Taiwan. ASE, founded in Kaohsiung in 1984, is the world's largest company that packages and tests chips for other companies. So the next time you hear about “advanced packaging,” think of a tall building: many chips, living close together, working as one.
paras_zh: 打開手機或電腦，你會看到綠色的板子上有一個個黑色的小方塊。那些方塊並不是晶片本身，而是封裝：一個堅固的外殼，晶片在裡面。封裝保護薄薄的矽不被碰撞、灰塵和濕氣傷害，也把晶片上很小的接點，接到電路板那個大得多的世界。
很長一段時間，封裝的工作就只有這些。一顆晶片放進一個封裝，一個個封裝焊在板子上，彼此相隔幾公分。可是晶片越來越快，晶片之間的那段路開始變得重要。負責思考的運算晶片送出資料，要穿過板子才到得了負責放資料的記憶體晶片。每走一趟，都要花時間和電。
那為什麼不乾脆做一顆很大的晶片，把所有東西都放在上面？因為晶片沒辦法無限制地變大。印電路的機器一次只能曝光大約 26 × 33 公釐的範圍。晶片越大，一片晶圓能做的顆數也越少，而且一粒灰塵就會毀掉更大的一塊。所以工程師走了另一條路：晶片維持小小的，但是讓它們靠得非常近。
第一種方法，是把沒有外殼的晶片並排放在一片薄薄的矽上，這片矽叫做中介層。它上面的線比電路板上的細得多，所以晶片幾乎可以貼在一起。這種做法叫做 2.5D 封裝。設計的人可以把叫做「小晶片」（chiplet）的小塊自由搭配，有點像玩樂高積木。
第二種方法，是把晶片一顆疊在另一顆上面，像大樓的樓層。叫做矽穿孔（TSV）的細銅柱直直穿過晶片，像電梯一樣。現在資料只要往上走幾層樓，不必橫越整個城市。線短了，訊號更快，浪費的電也更少。不過疊起來容易悶住熱，所以工程師要仔細規劃怎麼散熱。
封裝好之後，每一顆晶片都要經過測試才能出廠。封裝和測試合起來（簡稱封測）是台灣很大的產業。1984 年在高雄創立的日月光，是全世界最大的封裝測試代工公司。下次聽到「先進封裝」，就想像一棟高樓：很多顆晶片住得很近，一起工作，像一顆晶片一樣。
questions: What two jobs does a chip's package do?
Why don't engineers simply make one giant chip?
How is stacking chips like a tall building?
answers: It protects the chip from damage, and it connects the chip's tiny contacts to the circuit board.
The machine that prints circuits can only expose about 26 by 33 millimeters at a time, bigger chips mean fewer per wafer, and one speck of dust ruins a bigger piece.
The chips are like floors, and the TSVs are like elevators. Data goes up a few floors instead of traveling a long way across a board.

vocab.exzh: 晶片被封在一個黑色的封裝裡。

vocab.ex: The distance from my home to school is two kilometers.
vocab.exzh: 我家到學校的距離是兩公里。

vocab.ex: An elevator moves in a vertical line.
vocab.exzh: 電梯是沿著垂直的線移動。

vocab.exzh: 兩個朋友並排坐著。

vocab.exzh: 每一顆晶片賣出去之前都要測試。

options: A package with a chip inside

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Three packages, each with one chip. Follow the yellow dots along the gold lines: it is a long way from the logic chip to the memory.
parts.text_zh: 三個封裝，各裝一顆晶片。跟著黃色小點沿著金色的線走：從運算晶片到記憶體要走很遠。

parts.text_en: One package, five chips. They sit on an interposer, so close that the trip is ten times shorter in this model.
parts.text_zh: 一個封裝，五顆晶片。它們放在中介層上，靠得很近，在這個模型裡路程短了十倍。

parts.text_en: The memory chips become two towers, eight floors each. The gold posts are the elevators.
parts.text_zh: 記憶體晶片變成兩座塔，各有八層樓。金色的柱子就是電梯。

parts.text_en: From the bottom: circuit board, solder balls, substrate, tiny bumps, interposer, and the chips on top.
parts.text_zh: 從最下面開始：電路板、錫球、基板、細小的凸塊、中介層，最上面才是晶片。

lessons.parts_note_en: The distances in the panel are examples, but the pattern is real: each step brings the chips closer together.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 面板上的距離是舉例，但趨勢是真的：每換一種放法，晶片就靠得更近。

links_head.en: Where the chips come from, and where the limit comes from
links_head.zh: 晶片從哪裡來，那個上限又是怎麼來的

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體 第四課
links.en: How Do You Draw a Circuit Smaller Than a Virus?
links.zh: 怎麼畫出比病毒還小的電路？
links.note_en: Why one exposure is at most 26 × 33 millimeters.
links.note_zh: 為什麼一次曝光最大只有 26 × 33 公釐。

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體 第三課
links.en: How Does Sand Become a Chip?
links.note_en: Why bigger chips mean fewer chips on each wafer.
links.note_zh: 為什麼晶片越大，一片晶圓做得出來的顆數越少。

pack.eyebrow: Build a Package · 組一個封裝
pack.en: How many chips are in one package?
pack.zh: 一個封裝裡有幾顆晶片？
pack.lead_en: Put logic chips in the middle, add stacks of memory around them, and choose how many chips are in each stack. Count how many chips end up working as one.
pack.lead_zh: 把運算晶片放在中間，旁邊加上幾疊記憶體，再選每一疊有幾層。數數看，最後有幾顆晶片像一顆晶片一樣一起工作。
pack.note_en: This is a toy layout, not a real product. Stacks of 16 or more chips have been built. A single chip, by comparison, can be at most about 26 × 33 millimeters, the area of one exposure.
pack.note_zh: 這是示意的排法，不是哪一個真的產品。現實中已經有疊到 16 層以上的晶片。相比之下，單一顆晶片最大只能大約 26 × 33 公釐，也就是一次曝光的範圍。

facts.eyebrow: Packaging by the Numbers · 封裝的數字
facts.lead_en: Five numbers and names behind advanced packaging.
facts.lead_zh: 先進封裝背後的五個數字和名字。

items.en: The largest area one exposure can print. A single chip cannot be bigger than this.
items.zh: 一次曝光能印的最大範圍。單一顆晶片不能比這更大。

items.en: Bare chips placed next to one another on a silicon interposer, inside one package.
items.zh: 把沒有外殼的晶片並排放在矽中介層上，裝在同一個封裝裡。

items.en: Three-dimensional chips have been made by stacking as many as 16 or more chips.
items.zh: 3D 晶片已經做到把 16 顆以上的晶片疊在一起。

items.en: IBM began turning chips upside down and joining them with tiny balls of solder instead of wires.
items.zh: IBM 開始把晶片翻過來，用小小的錫球取代金屬線來連接。

items.en: ASE opened its first factory. It is now the world's largest packaging and testing company for other firms.
items.zh: 日月光的第一座工廠啟用。現在它是全世界最大的封裝測試代工公司。

culture_cards.title_en: An upside-down chip, LEGO bricks, a harbor city, and a long name
culture_cards.title_zh: 一顆翻過來的晶片、樂高積木、一座港都、一個很長的名字
culture_cards.lead_en: Four stories about putting chips together.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於「把晶片放在一起」的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: Early chips were joined to their packages by thin wires around the edges. In the 1960s IBM tried something different for its big computers: put tiny balls of solder on the chip, flip the chip face down, and melt the balls onto the package. This is called a flip chip. It allows many more connections, because the whole face of the chip can be used.
cards.body_zh: 早期的晶片是用邊緣一圈細細的金屬線接到封裝上。1960 年代，IBM 為了它的大型電腦試了不一樣的做法：在晶片上放小小的錫球，把晶片正面朝下翻過來，再把錫球熔接到封裝上。這叫做覆晶。這樣能做出多很多的接點，因為晶片的整個面都可以用。

cards.body_en: Instead of one big chip that does everything, designers can make several small chips, each good at one job, and place them side by side on an interposer. These small chips are called chiplets. People often compare them to LEGO bricks, because they can be mixed and matched.
cards.body_zh: 與其做一顆什麼都包的大晶片，設計的人可以做幾顆小晶片，每一顆專門做一件事，再把它們並排放在中介層上。這些小晶片叫做 chiplet。大家常把它們比做樂高積木，因為可以自由搭配。

cards.body_en: ASE was founded in 1984 by two brothers, who opened its first factory in Kaohsiung. Today its headquarters and main operations are still there, and it is the world's largest company that packages and tests chips for others. A chip designed in one country and made in Hsinchu or Tainan may well be packaged in Kaohsiung.
cards.body_zh: 日月光在 1984 年由一對兄弟創立，第一座工廠就在高雄。今天它的總部和主要的工廠還是在那裡，也是全世界最大的封裝測試代工公司。一顆在別的國家設計、在新竹或台南製造的晶片，很可能是在高雄封裝的。

cards.zh: 晶片放在晶圓上、再放在基板上
cards.body_en: You may see the word CoWoS in the news. It is TSMC's name for one kind of 2.5D packaging, and it simply describes the layers from top to bottom: Chip on Wafer on Substrate. The “wafer” in the middle is the silicon interposer.
cards.body_zh: 新聞裡常看到 CoWoS 這個字。它是台積電替一種 2.5D 封裝取的名字，意思就是從上到下的三層：晶片（Chip）放在晶圓（Wafer）上，再放在基板（Substrate）上。中間的那片「晶圓」就是矽中介層。

myths.myth_en: The black square on the circuit board is the chip.
myths.myth_zh: 電路板上的黑色方塊就是晶片。
myths.fact_en: It is the package. The chip is a thin piece of silicon sealed inside it.
myths.fact_zh: 那是封裝。晶片是封在裡面的一片薄薄的矽。

myths.myth_en: Packaging is just a box. It does not matter how it is done.
myths.myth_zh: 封裝只是一個盒子，怎麼做都沒差。
myths.fact_en: The package decides how close chips can be and how many connections they have, so it affects speed and power.
myths.fact_zh: 封裝決定晶片能靠多近、能有多少接點，所以會影響速度和耗電。

myths.myth_en: If we want more power, we can simply make one chip bigger and bigger.
myths.myth_zh: 想要更強，把一顆晶片越做越大就好了。
myths.fact_en: One exposure covers at most about 26 × 33 millimeters, and bigger chips mean fewer good chips from each wafer.
myths.fact_zh: 一次曝光最大只有大約 26 × 33 公釐；晶片越大，每片晶圓做得出來的好晶片也越少。

myths.myth_en: Stacking is always better than placing chips side by side.
myths.myth_zh: 疊起來一定比並排好。
myths.fact_en: Stacking makes the paths shortest, but it traps heat. Placing chips side by side keeps them cooler. Engineers choose what fits the job.
myths.fact_zh: 疊起來路最短，但容易悶住熱；並排比較好散熱。工程師會看用途來選。

tricks.body_en: It guards the chip and links it to the board.
tricks.body_zh: 保護晶片，並把它接到電路板上。

tricks.body_en: Apart on a board, side by side (2.5D), stacked (3D).
tricks.body_zh: 分開放在板子上、並排（2.5D）、疊起來（3D）。

tricks.body_en: They carry signals straight up through the chips.
tricks.body_zh: 它們帶著訊號直直往上穿過晶片。

tricks.body_en: But a tall stack needs a way to lose its heat.
tricks.body_zh: 不過疊得高，就要想辦法把熱散掉。

safety.en: Do not open phones, computers, or chargers to look for chips. They can hold a dangerous charge, and the parts are sharp.
safety.zh: 不要為了找晶片去拆手機、電腦或充電器。裡面可能還帶著危險的電，零件也很銳利。

safety.en: Old circuit boards from a recycling bin may have sharp edges. Ask an adult to check them first, and wash your hands afterward.
safety.zh: 回收來的舊電路板邊緣可能很利。先請大人檢查過，摸完要洗手。

safety.en: Small bricks and beads are a choking danger. Keep them away from little children.
safety.zh: 小積木和珠子可能噎到小小孩，不要讓他們拿到。

safety.en: Pick up string and bricks from the floor when you finish so that nobody trips.
safety.zh: 活動結束後，把地上的繩子和積木收好，免得有人絆倒。

materials.en: Building bricks in two colors (one color for logic, one for memory) and a large baseplate or a sheet of cardboard
materials.zh: 兩種顏色的積木（一種當運算晶片，一種當記憶體），和一塊大底板或厚紙板

materials.en: String, scissors, and a ruler
materials.zh: 繩子、剪刀和尺

steps.en: City 1: put one logic brick and four memory bricks far apart on the board. Use string to connect the logic brick to each memory brick.
steps.zh: 第一座城市：把一塊運算積木和四塊記憶體積木分開放在底板上，用繩子把運算積木和每一塊記憶體積木連起來。

steps.en: City 2: place the same five bricks side by side on a small plate. Connect them with string again.
steps.zh: 第二座城市：把同樣五塊積木並排放在一塊小板子上，再用繩子連一次。

steps.en: City 3: stack the four memory bricks into a tower beside the logic brick, and connect them.
steps.zh: 第三座城市：把四塊記憶體積木疊成一座塔，放在運算積木旁邊，再連起來。

steps.en: Measure all the string you used for each city. Which city needs the least?
steps.zh: 量一量每座城市用掉的繩子總長。哪一座用得最少？

activities.tip_en: The string is the wire. Less string means a shorter trip for the data, and less energy spent on the way.
activities.tip_zh: 繩子就是電線。繩子越短，資料走的路越短，路上花的電也越少。

materials.en: Ten small cards with numbers on them, and a timer
materials.zh: 十張寫著數字的小卡片，和一個計時器

materials.en: A classroom with space to move
materials.zh: 一間可以走動的教室

steps.en: One student is the logic chip, and another is the memory. First they stand at opposite ends of the classroom.
steps.zh: 一位同學當運算晶片，另一位當記憶體。先讓他們站在教室的兩頭。

steps.en: The logic chip carries the ten cards to the memory one at a time. Time how long it takes.
steps.zh: 運算晶片把十張卡片一張一張送到記憶體那裡。計時看要花多久。

steps.en: Now they stand side by side and do it again. Then try it with the memory sitting right in front of the logic chip.
steps.zh: 現在讓他們並排站，再做一次。接著讓記憶體就坐在運算晶片的正前方，再試一次。

steps.en: Compare the three times. Who got tired? What does that tell you about power?
steps.zh: 比較三次的時間。誰累了？這和「耗電」有什麼關係？

activities.tip_en: Walk, do not run. The point is the distance, not the speed of the runner.
activities.tip_zh: 用走的，不要跑。重點是距離，不是跑的人有多快。

sources.en: Packaging is the final stage of making a chip: the die is put in a case that prevents damage and corrosion and connects it to the circuit board; packaging is followed by testing
sources.zh: 封裝是製造晶片的最後階段：把晶粒放進能防止損傷與腐蝕的外殼，並連接到電路板；封裝之後進行測試

sources.en: 2.5D: several dies side by side on a silicon interposer in one package; placing dies side by side reduces heat buildup; chiplets combined LEGO-style; TSMC's CoWoS (Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate)
sources.zh: 2.5D：多顆晶粒並排放在矽中介層上、裝在同一個封裝；並排可減少積熱；小晶片像樂高一樣組合；台積電的 CoWoS

sources.en: 3D: stacking as many as 16 or more chips, connected vertically with through-silicon vias; shorter wires, less power
sources.zh: 3D：把 16 顆以上的晶片疊起來，用矽穿孔上下連接；線更短、更省電

sources.en: A through-silicon via is a vertical electrical connection that passes completely through a silicon wafer or die
sources.zh: 矽穿孔是完全穿過矽晶圓或晶粒的垂直電氣連接

sources.en: An interposer spreads or reroutes connections; it can be made of silicon or organic material
sources.zh: 中介層用來把接點展開或重新佈線；可以用矽或有機材料製作

sources.en: Flip chip: solder bumps on the chip, which is flipped face down; introduced commercially by IBM in the 1960s
sources.zh: 覆晶：在晶片上做錫球凸塊，再把晶片正面朝下翻過來；1960 年代由 IBM 商業化

sources.en: The EUV exposure field is 26 × 33 mm
sources.zh: EUV 一次曝光的範圍是 26 × 33 公釐

sources.en: ASE: founded in 1984 with its first factory in Kaohsiung; headquarters in Kaohsiung; the largest outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) provider according to Gartner
sources.zh: 日月光：1984 年創立，第一座工廠在高雄；總部在高雄；依 Gartner 是最大的封裝測試代工（OSAT）業者

lessons.title: What Is HBM, and Why Does AI Need It?
lessons.title_zh: HBM 是什麼？AI 為什麼需要它？
lessons.blurb_en: An AI chip can calculate very fast, but it often has to wait for its data. HBM is memory stacked like a tower right beside the chip and joined to it by a road with more than a thousand lanes. In 3D, compare ordinary memory with four generations of HBM, then work out how many movies it could move in one second.
lessons.blurb_zh: AI 晶片算得很快，卻常常要等資料。HBM 是像高塔一樣疊起來的記憶體，就放在晶片旁邊，中間是一條有上千個車道的路。在 3D 裡比較一般記憶體和四代 HBM，再算算它一秒可以搬幾部電影。
lessons.big_idea_en: A fast chip is no use if its data arrives slowly. HBM, short for High Bandwidth Memory, stacks memory chips into a tower, connects the floors with tiny elevators called TSVs, and sets the tower right next to the logic chip. More than a thousand data lines join them, like a very wide, very short highway, so huge amounts of data move at once.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 資料送得慢，晶片再快也沒用。HBM 是「高頻寬記憶體」（High Bandwidth Memory）的縮寫：把記憶體晶片疊成一座塔，用叫做矽穿孔的小電梯連接每一層，再把塔緊貼著運算晶片放。上千條資料線把兩邊連起來，像一條又寬又短的高速公路，一次就能送很多資料。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Start with “Ordinary memory”: the memory chips are far across the board, and the road has few lanes. Then choose HBM. The memory becomes a tower beside the blue logic chip, and the road becomes short and wide. Pick a generation on the right to see the lanes, the floors, and the speed change.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。先看「一般記憶體」：記憶體晶片在板子的另一頭，路上沒幾個車道。再選 HBM：記憶體變成藍色運算晶片旁邊的一座塔，路變得又短又寬。在右邊選世代，看車道、樓層和速度怎麼變。

far.en: Ordinary memory sits in its own packages, some distance from the logic chip. Each memory chip has only a few dozen data lines, and the trip is long. The logic chip finishes its work and waits.
far.zh: 一般的記憶體各有自己的封裝，離運算晶片有一段距離。每顆記憶體晶片只有幾十條資料線，路又長。運算晶片算完了，只能等。

hbm1.en: The first HBM became a standard in 2013. Four memory chips are stacked, and 1,024 data lines join the stack to the logic chip. That is 32 times as many as an ordinary graphics memory chip has.
hbm1.zh: 第一代 HBM 在 2013 年成為標準。四層記憶體疊在一起，用 1,024 條資料線接到運算晶片，是一顆一般顯示卡記憶體的 32 倍。

hbm2.en: HBM2 arrived in 2016. The road is still 1,024 lanes wide, but each lane carries data more than twice as fast, and the tower can be eight floors tall.
hbm2.zh: HBM2 在 2016 年推出。路還是 1,024 個車道，但每個車道送資料的速度快了兩倍多，塔也可以疊到八層。

hbm3.en: HBM3 came in 2022. Each lane is faster again, and one stack can move about 819 gigabytes every second.
hbm3.zh: HBM3 在 2022 年推出。每個車道又更快了，一疊每秒能送大約 819 GB。

hbm4.en: HBM4, set as a standard in 2025, doubles the road to 2,048 lanes, and the tower can have 16 floors. One stack can move about 2,048 gigabytes every second.
hbm4.zh: 2025 年訂出標準的 HBM4，把路加寬一倍到 2,048 個車道，塔也可以疊到 16 層。一疊每秒能送大約 2,048 GB。

legend.en: Blue: the logic chip, which does the calculating
legend.zh: 藍色：運算晶片，負責計算

legend.en: Purple: memory chips (stacked, in HBM)
legend.zh: 紫色：記憶體晶片（HBM 是疊起來的）

legend.en: Gray road with lane lines: the data lines. One lane in the model stands for 64 real data lines
legend.zh: 有車道線的灰色路面：資料線。模型裡的一個車道代表 64 條真的資料線

legend.en: Small cars: data on the move (yellow going one way, blue the other)
legend.zh: 小車子：正在移動的資料（黃色往一邊、藍色往另一邊）

lab.scale_en: A teaching diagram, not to scale. The numbers of data lines, floors, and gigabytes per second come from the published HBM standards. The road, the cars, and the distances are only pictures: real data lines are thin wires inside the interposer, and data is electrical signals, not cars. The ordinary memory shown is graphics memory, whose chips each have 32 data lines; it is drawn with a single lane.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意圖，不是真實比例。資料線數、樓層數和每秒幾 GB 來自公開的 HBM 標準。路、車子和距離都只是比喻：真的資料線是中介層裡的細線，資料是電的訊號，不是車子。圖裡的一般記憶體是顯示卡記憶體，每顆晶片 32 條資料線，模型裡畫成一個車道。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The figures for each generation follow the table in Wikipedia, “High Bandwidth Memory”, which cites the JEDEC standards. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；各代的數字依維基百科「High Bandwidth Memory」條目的規格表（引自 JEDEC 標準）。

paras: Imagine the best cook in the world working in a kitchen where the refrigerator is at the other end of the street. The cook is fast, but most of the time is spent walking to fetch the eggs. A chip that runs AI has the same trouble. It can do an enormous number of calculations each second, but only if the numbers it needs arrive in time.

Those numbers are kept in memory chips. In an ordinary computer, the memory sits in its own packages some distance from the logic chip, and each memory chip talks through only a few dozen data lines. For everyday work that is fine. For AI, which moves mountains of data, the logic chip ends up waiting. The memory cannot deliver fast enough.

HBM was made to fix this. The letters stand for High Bandwidth Memory. Bandwidth means how much data can move in one second. Engineers did three things. First, they stacked memory chips on top of one another, like the floors of a tower. Second, they ran tiny copper posts, called TSVs, straight through the stack, like elevators, so every floor is connected.

Third, they moved the tower right next to the logic chip, on the same interposer you met in the last lesson. Because the two are so close, they can be joined by a huge number of very short wires. The first HBM had 1,024 data lines for each stack. Think of a highway with more than a thousand lanes that is very, very short.

HBM became an industry standard in 2013, and it has grown quickly since. Each new generation sends data faster through every lane, and the towers get taller: 4 floors, then 8, 12, and 16. The newest standard, HBM4, doubles the highway to 2,048 lanes. One HBM4 stack can move about 2,048 gigabytes in a single second.

That is why you now hear about HBM in the news. An AI chip usually has several HBM towers standing around it, feeding it data all day. The memory is no longer far down the street. The refrigerator has moved right beside the cook, and it has a thousand doors.
paras_zh: 想像全世界最厲害的廚師，在一間廚房裡工作，可是冰箱在街的另一頭。廚師手腳很快，但大部分的時間都花在走路去拿雞蛋。跑 AI 的晶片也有一樣的麻煩：它每秒能做非常非常多次計算，但前提是它需要的數字要及時送到。
這些數字放在記憶體晶片裡。一般的電腦，記憶體各有自己的封裝，和運算晶片隔著一段距離，而且每顆記憶體晶片只透過幾十條資料線來溝通。平常的工作這樣就夠了。可是 AI 要搬動像山一樣多的資料，運算晶片最後只能乾等，因為記憶體送得不夠快。
HBM 就是為了解決這件事做出來的。這三個字母是 High Bandwidth Memory，高頻寬記憶體；「頻寬」的意思是一秒鐘能送多少資料。工程師做了三件事。第一，把記憶體晶片一顆顆疊起來，像一座塔的樓層。第二，用叫做矽穿孔（TSV）的細銅柱直直穿過整疊晶片，像電梯一樣，讓每一層都連得到。
第三，把這座塔搬到運算晶片的正旁邊，放在上一課認識的中介層上。因為兩邊靠得這麼近，就可以用非常多條很短的線把它們連起來。第一代 HBM 每一疊就有 1,024 條資料線。想像一條有一千多個車道、卻非常非常短的高速公路。
HBM 在 2013 年成為業界標準，之後進步得很快。每一代，每個車道送資料的速度都更快，塔也越疊越高：4 層、8 層、12 層、16 層。最新的標準 HBM4，把高速公路加寬一倍到 2,048 個車道。一疊 HBM4 一秒鐘大約能送 2,048 GB 的資料。
所以現在新聞裡常聽到 HBM。一顆 AI 晶片的旁邊通常站著好幾座 HBM 的塔，整天不停地餵資料給它。記憶體不再遠在街的另一頭了：冰箱已經搬到廚師身邊，而且有一千個門。

band.en: How many movies in one second?
band.lead_en: Suppose one movie file is 5 gigabytes. Choose a generation of HBM and how many stacks stand beside the chip, and see how many movies' worth of data they could move every second.
band.lead_zh: 假設一部電影的檔案是 5 GB。選一代 HBM、選晶片旁邊放幾疊，看看它們每秒可以搬動相當於幾部電影的資料。
band.note_en: The 5-gigabyte movie and the home internet speeds are examples. The gigabytes per second for each generation are the top figures in the standards for one stack; real products may run below them.
band.note_zh: 5 GB 的電影和家用網路的速度都是舉例。各代每秒幾 GB 是標準裡一疊的最高數字，實際的產品可能比較低。

facts.eyebrow: HBM by the Numbers · HBM 的數字
facts.lead_en: Six numbers from the HBM standards.
facts.lead_zh: HBM 標準裡的六個數字。

items.en: HBM was adopted as an industry standard in October 2013.
items.zh: HBM 在 2013 年 10 月成為業界標準。

items.en: The width of the road for one stack in the first three generations.
items.zh: 前三代，每一疊的「路寬」。

items.en: An ordinary graphics memory chip has 32 data lines. An HBM stack has 32 times as many.
items.zh: 一顆一般的顯示卡記憶體有 32 條資料線，一疊 HBM 是它的 32 倍。

items.en: The tallest stack in the newest standards: sixteen memory chips, one on top of another.
items.zh: 最新標準裡最高的一疊：十六顆記憶體晶片一顆疊一顆。

items.en: The 2025 standard doubles the road.
items.zh: 2025 年的標準把路加寬一倍。

items.en: From 128 gigabytes a second in 2013 to 2,048 in 2025, for a single stack.
items.zh: 單一疊的速度，從 2013 年的每秒 128 GB 到 2025 年的 2,048 GB。

culture_cards.title_en: A word, a committee, a tower, and three makers
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個詞、一個委員會、一座塔、三家公司
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories behind three letters.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 三個字母背後的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: Bandwidth tells you how much data can pass in one second. You can raise it in two ways: add more lanes, or make each lane faster. HBM does both. That is why it has “High Bandwidth” in its name.
cards.body_zh: 頻寬告訴你一秒鐘能通過多少資料。要提高它有兩個辦法：增加車道，或讓每個車道更快。HBM 兩樣都做，所以名字裡才有「高頻寬」。

cards.body_en: HBM was first developed by Samsung, AMD, and SK Hynix, and in October 2013 an industry group called JEDEC adopted it as a standard. A standard means that memory from different makers fits the same chips, the way any plug fits a socket made to the same standard.
cards.body_zh: HBM 最早是三星、超微（AMD）和 SK 海力士開發的；2013 年 10 月，叫做 JEDEC 的產業組織把它訂成標準。有了標準，不同公司做的記憶體就能配同樣的晶片，就像照同一個標準做的插頭都插得進插座。

cards.body_en: The first HBM stacks had four memory chips. Later generations went to eight, then twelve, then sixteen. As the tower grows, each chip has to be thinner, and the tiny posts that run through them must line up from floor to floor.
cards.body_zh: 第一代 HBM 疊四顆記憶體晶片，後來變成八顆、十二顆、十六顆。塔越高，每一顆晶片就要越薄，穿過它們的細柱也要一層一層對得剛剛好。

cards.body_en: In 2025 the world's largest makers of HBM were SK Hynix and Samsung of South Korea and Micron of the United States. The towers are then joined to logic chips by advanced packaging, the subject of the last lesson.
cards.body_zh: 2025 年全世界最大的 HBM 製造商，是南韓的 SK 海力士和三星，以及美國的美光。這些塔接著要靠先進封裝（上一課的主題）和運算晶片接在一起。

myths.myth_en: HBM is a kind of AI chip that does the thinking.
myths.myth_zh: HBM 是一種負責思考的 AI 晶片。
myths.fact_en: HBM is memory. It holds the data and hands it over quickly. The calculating is done by the logic chip beside it.
myths.fact_zh: HBM 是記憶體，負責放資料、並且很快地交出去。計算是旁邊的運算晶片做的。

myths.myth_en: High bandwidth just means the memory holds more.
myths.myth_zh: 高頻寬就是記憶體裝得比較多。
myths.fact_en: Bandwidth is about speed of delivery: how much data moves each second. How much the memory holds is called capacity.
myths.fact_zh: 頻寬講的是送得多快：每秒搬多少資料。能裝多少叫做容量。

myths.myth_en: A faster logic chip always makes the whole computer faster.
myths.myth_zh: 運算晶片越快，整台電腦就一定越快。
myths.fact_en: Not if it has to wait for data. A fast cook with a faraway refrigerator is still slow.
myths.fact_zh: 如果它要等資料，就不一定。冰箱在很遠的地方，再快的廚師也快不起來。

myths.myth_en: HBM is just ordinary memory with a new name.
myths.myth_zh: HBM 只是一般記憶體換個名字。
myths.fact_en: It is built differently: chips stacked with TSVs, set beside the logic chip, and joined by over a thousand data lines.
myths.fact_zh: 它的做法不一樣：用矽穿孔把晶片疊起來、放在運算晶片旁邊、用上千條資料線相連。

tricks.body_en: HBM is memory moved right next to the chip.
tricks.body_zh: HBM 就是搬到晶片旁邊的記憶體。

tricks.body_en: Memory chips are stacked, and TSVs connect the floors.
tricks.body_zh: 記憶體晶片疊起來，矽穿孔連接每一層。

tricks.body_en: 1,024 data lines in each stack, and 2,048 in HBM4.
tricks.body_zh: 每一疊 1,024 條資料線，HBM4 是 2,048 條。

tricks.body_en: That is what bandwidth means.
tricks.body_zh: 這就是頻寬的意思。

safety.en: Do not open computers, graphics cards, or servers to look for memory. They can be damaged by a tiny spark from your fingers, and some parts stay charged.
safety.zh: 不要為了找記憶體去拆電腦、顯示卡或伺服器。手指上一點點靜電就可能弄壞零件，有些零件還帶著電。

safety.en: In the highway game, walk. Mark the lanes clearly so that nobody bumps into anyone else.
safety.zh: 玩高速公路遊戲的時候用走的。把車道標清楚，免得互相撞到。

safety.en: Keep small cards and tokens away from little children.
safety.zh: 小卡片和代幣不要讓小小孩拿到。

materials.en: Forty small cards (the data), a timer, and tape to mark lanes on the floor
materials.zh: 四十張小卡片（資料）、計時器，和在地上貼車道用的膠帶

materials.en: Two tables: one is the memory, one is the logic chip
materials.zh: 兩張桌子：一張當記憶體，一張當運算晶片

steps.en: Round 1: put the tables far apart with one lane between them. One student at a time carries one card. How many cards arrive in one minute?
steps.zh: 第一回合：兩張桌子離很遠，中間只有一個車道。一次只能一位同學拿一張卡片走過去。一分鐘送到幾張？

steps.en: Round 2: keep the distance, but mark four lanes. Four students can walk at once.
steps.zh: 第二回合：距離不變，但是貼出四個車道，可以四位同學同時走。

steps.en: Round 3: push the tables close together and keep the four lanes.
steps.zh: 第三回合：把兩張桌子推近，維持四個車道。

steps.en: Write down the cards per minute for each round. That number is the bandwidth. Which change helped more: more lanes, or a shorter road?
steps.zh: 記下每一回合每分鐘送到幾張，這個數字就是頻寬。哪一種改變幫助比較大：車道變多，還是路變短？

activities.tip_en: HBM does both at once: far more lanes, and a much shorter road.
activities.tip_zh: HBM 兩樣一起做：車道多很多，路也短很多。

materials.en: Sixteen squares of cardboard, all the same size
materials.zh: 十六片一樣大的方形厚紙板

materials.en: Drinking straws, a hole punch, and a marker
materials.zh: 吸管、打洞器和麥克筆

steps.en: Punch four holes in the same places on every square. These are the TSVs.
steps.zh: 在每一片紙板的同樣位置打四個洞，這些就是矽穿孔。

steps.en: Write a different number on each square. These are the data.
steps.zh: 在每一片上寫一個不同的數字，這些就是資料。

steps.en: Thread the straws through the holes to stack four squares, then eight, then sixteen.
steps.zh: 把吸管穿過洞，先疊四片，再疊八片，最後疊十六片。

steps.en: What gets harder as the tower grows? What would happen if one hole were in the wrong place?
steps.zh: 塔越高，什麼事變得越難？如果有一個洞打歪了，會怎麼樣？

activities.tip_en: In a real stack, a great many posts must line up through every chip. That is one reason tall stacks are hard to make.
activities.tip_zh: 真的堆疊裡，非常多根細柱要穿過每一顆晶片、全部對準。這是高的堆疊很難做的原因之一。

sources.en: HBM: an interface for 3D-stacked memory, first developed by Samsung, AMD, and SK Hynix; adopted by JEDEC as an industry standard in October 2013; HBM2 in January 2016
sources.zh: HBM：3D 堆疊記憶體的介面，最早由三星、超微與 SK 海力士開發；2013 年 10 月由 JEDEC 訂為業界標準；HBM2 於 2016 年 1 月

sources.en: Specification table: HBM (2013) 1,024 bits, 4 dies, 128 GB/s; HBM2 (2016) 8 dies, 307 GB/s; HBM3 (2022) 12 dies, 819 GB/s; HBM4 (April 2025) 2,048 bits, 16 dies, 2,048 GB/s per stack
The HBM bus is very wide: 1,024 bits for a stack, compared with 32 bits for a GDDR memory chip; an interposer connects the memory and the processor and keeps them physically close
sources.zh: HBM 的匯流排很寬：一疊 1,024 位元，GDDR 記憶體每顆 32 位元；用中介層連接記憶體與處理器，讓兩者靠得很近

sources.en: In 2025 the largest makers of HBM included SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, and Micron Technology; demand has risen sharply because of AI
sources.zh: 2025 年最大的 HBM 製造商包括 SK 海力士、三星電子與美光；因為 AI，需求大幅上升

sources.en: A through-silicon via is a vertical electrical connection that passes completely through a silicon die
sources.zh: 矽穿孔是完全穿過矽晶粒的垂直電氣連接

lessons.title: How Did Taiwan Become a Chip Island?
lessons.blurb_en: A chip is designed, made, and packaged by different companies, and Taiwan has important ones for every step. On a 3D map, follow one chip from Hsinchu to Tainan to Kaohsiung and out to the world, then drag a timeline from 1973 to see how the industry grew. Finish by sorting companies by the job they do.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一顆晶片由不同的公司負責設計、製造和封裝，而每一段台灣都有重要的公司。在 3D 地圖上跟著一顆晶片從新竹到台南、再到高雄，最後送往全世界；再從 1973 年開始拉時間軸，看這個產業怎麼長大。最後玩個小遊戲，分分看哪家公司做哪一段。
lessons.big_idea_en: Making a chip takes three big jobs: designing it, manufacturing it, and packaging and testing it. In 1987 a company in Taiwan chose to do only the manufacturing, for anyone who had a design. That idea, the foundry, changed how the world makes chips. Today Taiwan has important companies for all three jobs, gathered in a few science parks.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 做出一顆晶片有三件大事：設計、製造、封裝測試。1987 年，台灣有一家公司決定只做「製造」這一段，誰有設計就幫誰做。這個點子叫做晶圓代工，改變了全世界做晶片的方式。今天，這三件事台灣都有重要的公司，而且集中在幾個科學園區裡。

lab.title_en: One Chip's Trip Across the Island
lab.how_en: Drag to turn the map, and scroll or pinch to zoom. In “A chip's journey,” watch a glowing chip travel through the three jobs and then leave for the world; press a step to see it again. Then choose “Timeline” and drag the year from 1970 to 2005. Places light up on the map as things happen there.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉地圖，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。在「晶片的旅程」，看一顆發亮的晶片走過三段工作、最後飛向全世界；按任何一步可以再看一次。再選「時間軸」，把年份從 1970 拉到 2005，哪裡發生了事情，地圖上的那個地方就會亮起來。

steps.text_en: Engineers at a design company draw the circuit on computers: billions of transistors and the wires between them. A company that only designs chips is called fabless, because it has no factory. MediaTek, in Hsinchu, is one.
steps.text_zh: 設計公司的工程師在電腦上畫出電路：幾十億個電晶體，和它們之間的連線。只做設計、沒有工廠的公司叫做無廠半導體公司（fabless）。總部在新竹的聯發科就是其中一家。

steps.text_en: The design goes to a foundry, a company that manufactures chips for others. In a wafer fab in a science park, the pattern is printed onto silicon wafers layer by layer, as you saw in Lessons 3 and 4.
steps.text_zh: 設計圖送到晶圓代工廠，也就是替別人製造晶片的公司。在科學園區的晶圓廠裡，圖案一層一層印到矽晶圓上，就像第三、四課看到的那樣。

steps.text_en: The wafers travel to a packaging and testing company. There the chips are cut apart, put into packages, sometimes stacked together as in Lesson 6, and tested one by one.
steps.text_zh: 晶圓接著送到封裝測試公司。晶片在那裡被切開、放進封裝，有時像第六課那樣疊在一起，再一顆一顆測試。

steps.text_en: The finished chips leave Taiwan for factories that build phones, computers, cars, and servers. This route is only an example: every chip has its own path, and many paths cross other countries too.
steps.text_zh: 做好的晶片離開台灣，送到組裝手機、電腦、汽車和伺服器的工廠。這條路線只是一個例子：每顆晶片都有自己的路，很多還會經過別的國家。

events.en: ITRI, a government research institute, is founded.
events.zh: 工業技術研究院（工研院）成立。

events.en: Engineers are sent to RCA in the United States to learn how to make chips.
events.zh: 工程師被派到美國 RCA 公司學習製造積體電路。

events.en: UMC, Taiwan's first chip company, is spun off from ITRI.

paras: Taiwan is a small island, yet people all over the world call it a chip island. Phones, computers, cars, and the servers that run AI depend on chips that passed through Taiwan. How did this happen? It did not happen by luck, and it did not happen quickly. It took about fifty years, and it began with a plan.

In 1973 the government founded a research institute called ITRI in Hsinchu. A year later, a small group of officials and engineers met to discuss how Taiwan could start making integrated circuits. In 1976 teams of young engineers were sent to RCA, a company in the United States, to learn how. They came home and built a demonstration factory, and it worked well.

The next step was to turn research into companies. In 1980 UMC was spun off from ITRI and became Taiwan's first chip company. In the same year Hsinchu Science Park opened beside two universities, so that companies, engineers, and students could be close together. Today hundreds of companies have their homes in that park.

Then came the big idea. In those days, a chip company did everything itself: it designed its chips and also built the expensive factories to make them. In 1987 Morris Chang founded TSMC to do only one part. It would manufacture chips for any company that had a design, and it would not design chips of its own. This kind of company is called a foundry.

The foundry changed the industry. Now a small team with a good idea could design a chip without building a factory. Design companies, called fabless companies, grew up around the world. And Taiwan filled in the other steps as well: design companies such as MediaTek in Hsinchu, and packaging and testing companies such as ASE in Kaohsiung.

So a chip's trip can look like this: designed in one place, manufactured in a science park, packaged and tested in another city, and then shipped to the world. Hsinchu, Taichung, Tainan, and Kaohsiung all lie along the west coast of one small island, and that closeness helps. The chip island was built by many people over many years, one step at a time.
paras_zh: 台灣是一座小島，全世界卻有很多人叫它「晶片島」。手機、電腦、汽車，還有跑 AI 的伺服器，都靠著經過台灣的晶片。這是怎麼來的？不是靠運氣，也不是一下子就發生的。它花了大約五十年，而且是從一個計畫開始的。
1973 年，政府在新竹成立了一個研究機構，叫做工業技術研究院（工研院）。隔年，一小群官員和工程師開會，討論台灣要怎麼開始做積體電路。1976 年，一批批年輕的工程師被派到美國的 RCA 公司去學。他們回來之後蓋了一座示範工廠，而且做得很成功。
下一步是把研究變成公司。1980 年，聯華電子（聯電）從工研院獨立出來，成為台灣第一家積體電路公司。同一年，新竹科學園區在兩所大學旁邊成立，讓公司、工程師和學生靠得很近。今天有好幾百家公司把家安在這個園區裡。
接著是那個重要的點子。那個年代，一家晶片公司什麼都自己來：自己設計晶片，也自己蓋昂貴的工廠來製造。1987 年，張忠謀創辦台積電，只做其中一段：誰有設計，它就幫誰製造，自己不設計晶片。這種公司叫做晶圓代工廠。
晶圓代工改變了整個產業。從此以後，一個有好點子的小團隊不用蓋工廠也能設計晶片。只做設計的「無廠半導體公司」在世界各地冒出來。而其他幾段，台灣也補上了：做設計的公司，例如新竹的聯發科；做封裝測試的公司，例如高雄的日月光。
所以一顆晶片的旅程可能是這樣：在一個地方設計，在科學園區製造，到另一個城市封裝測試，然後送往全世界。新竹、台中、台南、高雄都在同一座小島的西岸，這種「近」很有幫助。晶片島是很多人花了很多年，一步一步蓋起來的。

What was new about TSMC in 1987?

answers: Designing the chip, manufacturing it, and packaging and testing it.
It only manufactured chips for other companies and did not design chips of its own. It was the world's first company of this kind, called a foundry.
Because a chip has to pass from one company to the next. When they are close, people, wafers, and ideas can move between them quickly.

culture_cards.eyebrow: Chip Island Stories · 晶片島的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A meeting, a classroom abroad, a park beside two universities, and one bold idea
culture_cards.title_zh: 一場會議、一間海外的教室、兩所大學旁的園區、一個大膽的點子
culture_cards.lead_en: Four moments that shaped the island.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 塑造這座島的四個時刻。

cards.body_en: In 1974 a small group met to talk about Taiwan's future: the minister of economic affairs, Sun Yun-suan, several other officials, the president of ITRI, and Pan Wen-Yuan, a research director from RCA. They talked about how Taiwan could build a semiconductor industry. Taiwan's chip industry counts its start from that year.
cards.body_zh: 1974 年，一小群人坐下來談台灣的未來：經濟部長孫運璿、幾位官員、工研院院長，還有 RCA 研究室主任潘文淵。他們討論的是台灣要怎麼發展半導體產業。台灣的半導體產業，就從這一年算起。

cards.body_en: In 1976 RCA agreed to transfer its chipmaking technology. ITRI sent four teams of engineers to train at RCA in the United States. Back home, they built a demonstration factory, and it reached higher yields than RCA's own factories.
cards.body_zh: 1976 年，RCA 同意把製造晶片的技術轉移過來。工研院派了四組工程師到美國 RCA 受訓。回來之後，他們蓋了一座示範工廠，良率比 RCA 自己的工廠還高。

cards.body_en: The idea for Hsinchu Science Park came in 1976: build a place like Silicon Valley, next to National Tsing Hua University and National Chiao Tung University, so that companies and classrooms would be neighbors. The park was established on December 15, 1980.
cards.body_zh: 新竹科學園區的構想出現在 1976 年：仿照矽谷，把園區蓋在清華大學和交通大學旁邊，讓公司和教室當鄰居。園區在 1980 年 12 月 15 日成立。

cards.body_en: Morris Chang had worked at Texas Instruments for 25 years before he was invited to Taiwan to lead ITRI. In 1987 he founded TSMC as a joint venture of the government, ITRI, and private investors. It would manufacture chips for others and design none of its own. That way of working became a model for the whole industry.
cards.body_zh: 張忠謀在德州儀器工作了 25 年，之後受邀到台灣擔任工研院院長。1987 年，他創辦台積電，由政府、工研院和民間一起出資。這家公司只替別人製造晶片，自己不設計。這種做法後來成了整個產業的模式。

myths.myth_en: One company makes a chip from start to finish.
myths.myth_zh: 一顆晶片從頭到尾都是同一家公司做的。
myths.fact_en: Usually not. One company designs it, another manufactures it, and often a third packages and tests it.
myths.fact_zh: 通常不是。一家設計，另一家製造，常常還有第三家負責封裝和測試。

myths.myth_en: Taiwan's chip industry appeared suddenly a few years ago.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣的晶片產業是這幾年突然冒出來的。
myths.fact_en: It grew step by step over about fifty years, starting with a research institute in 1973.
myths.fact_zh: 它是花了大約五十年一步一步長大的，從 1973 年的一個研究機構開始。

myths.myth_en: A foundry designs the chips it makes.
myths.myth_zh: 晶圓代工廠自己設計它做的晶片。
myths.fact_en: A foundry manufactures chips that other companies designed. That is exactly what makes it a foundry.
myths.fact_zh: 晶圓代工廠製造的是別的公司設計的晶片，這正是「代工」的意思。

myths.myth_en: Chips made in Taiwan are made only from things found in Taiwan.
myths.myth_zh: 台灣做的晶片，用的都是台灣自己的東西。
myths.fact_en: Chipmaking is a worldwide effort. The machines, materials, designs, and customers come from many countries, as you saw in Lessons 3 and 4.
myths.fact_zh: 做晶片要靠全世界一起合作。機器、材料、設計和客戶來自很多國家，就像第三、四課看到的那樣。

tricks.body_en: Three jobs, usually done by three kinds of companies.
tricks.body_zh: 三段工作，通常由三種公司來做。

tricks.title_zh: 代工廠製造，無廠公司設計
tricks.body_en: One has the factory. The other has the idea.
tricks.body_zh: 一個有工廠，一個有點子。

tricks.title_zh: 先研究、再開公司、再蓋園區
tricks.body_en: 1973, 1980, and onward: each step built on the last.

safety.en: A science park is a workplace, not a playground. Visit only on an arranged tour, and stay with your teacher.
safety.zh: 科學園區是上班的地方，不是遊樂場。只在安排好的參訪時進去，並且跟緊老師。

safety.en: When you interview a family member about work, ask first, and do not share anything that their company keeps secret.
safety.zh: 訪問家人工作上的事情之前要先問過，公司要保密的事情不要寫出來。

safety.en: Use scissors and pins carefully when you make your map.
safety.zh: 做地圖的時候，小心使用剪刀和圖釘。

materials.en: A sheet of paper and a pencil for each team, and three tables
materials.zh: 每隊一張紙和一支鉛筆，還有三張桌子

materials.en: Signs for the tables: Design, Manufacture, Package and Test
materials.zh: 三張桌子的牌子：設計、製造、封裝測試

steps.en: At the Design table, one student draws a simple pattern of five shapes and passes the paper on.
steps.zh: 在「設計」桌，一位同學畫出由五個形狀組成的簡單圖案，再把紙傳下去。

steps.en: At the Manufacture table, the next student copies the pattern exactly, four times, on a new sheet (four chips on one wafer).
steps.zh: 在「製造」桌，下一位同學把圖案一模一樣地畫四次在新的紙上（一片晶圓上四顆晶片）。

steps.en: At the Package and Test table, the last student cuts the four apart, checks each against the design, and throws away any that are wrong.
steps.zh: 在「封裝測試」桌，最後一位同學把四顆剪開，一顆一顆對照設計圖檢查，把錯的丟掉。

steps.en: Count the good chips. Then talk about it: what happens to the whole team if one table is slow, or far away?
steps.zh: 數一數有幾顆好晶片。再討論：如果有一張桌子很慢、或離得很遠，整隊會怎麼樣？

activities.tip_en: Nobody at the Manufacture table changes the design. That is the foundry's promise.
activities.tip_zh: 「製造」桌的人不會去改設計。這就是晶圓代工的承諾。

steps.en: Use string to show one chip's trip: design, manufacture, package and test.
steps.zh: 用線拉出一顆晶片的旅程：設計、製造、封裝測試。

steps.en: Beside each city, write one date from the timeline and what happened there.
steps.zh: 在每個城市旁邊寫上時間軸裡的一個年份，和那裡發生了什麼事。

steps.en: Ask at home: does anyone in your family, or a neighbor, work with chips or electronics? Which of the three jobs is theirs?
steps.zh: 回家問問看：家人或鄰居裡，有沒有人做和晶片或電子產品有關的工作？他們做的是三段裡的哪一段？

activities.tip_en: From Changhua, Taichung is right next door, and Hsinchu is up the coast to the north. You live in the middle of the chip island.
activities.tip_zh: 從彰化出發，台中就在隔壁，新竹在北邊的海岸線上。你就住在晶片島的中間。

lessons.title: Why Do Chips Get Hot?
lessons.blurb_en: Your phone warms up when you play a game, and a laptop sometimes roars with its fan. Where does the heat come from? In a 3D model, give a chip more work, then add a heat sink and a fan, and watch its temperature and speed. Then use two sliders to see why a little less voltage saves a lot of power.
lessons.blurb_zh: 玩遊戲的時候手機會變燙，筆電的風扇有時候呼呼地轉。這些熱是從哪裡來的？在 3D 模型裡給晶片更多工作，再加上散熱片和風扇，看它的溫度和速度怎麼變。接著拉兩條滑桿，看看為什麼電壓只降一點點，就能省下很多電。
lessons.big_idea_en: A chip turns the electrical energy it uses into heat. Every time a transistor switches, a tiny bit of energy is spent, and a chip has billions of transistors switching billions of times a second. The harder the chip works, the more heat it makes. That heat must be carried away, or the chip protects itself by slowing down.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 晶片用掉的電能，會變成熱。電晶體每開關一次，就花掉一點點能量；而一顆晶片有幾十億個電晶體，每秒開關幾十億次。晶片越忙，發的熱越多。這些熱一定要帶走，不然晶片就會放慢速度來保護自己。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. First choose how hard the chip is working: idle, playing a video, or running a game. Then choose how it is cooled: nothing at all, a heat sink, or a heat sink with a fan. The chip changes color as it warms up, and the orange dots show heat leaving. Watch what happens to the speed when the chip gets too hot.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。先選晶片有多忙：待機、看影片，還是玩遊戲。再選怎麼散熱：什麼都不裝、裝散熱片，或是散熱片加風扇。晶片越熱，顏色就越紅；橘色的小點代表正在離開的熱。注意看晶片太熱的時候，速度會怎麼樣。

none.en: With nothing on top, heat can leave only from the chip's own small surface. That is fine for light work, but not for heavy work.
none.zh: 上面什麼都沒有的時候，熱只能從晶片自己小小的表面離開。工作輕的時候沒問題，工作重就不行了。

sink.en: A heat sink is a piece of metal with many fins. The fins give the heat far more surface from which to pass into the air.
sink.zh: 散熱片是一塊有很多鰭片的金屬。鰭片讓熱有大得多的表面可以傳到空氣裡。

fan.en: The fan does not make cold. It pushes the warmed air away, so cooler air can take its place and carry off more heat.
fan.zh: 風扇不會製造冷氣。它把被加熱的空氣吹走，讓比較涼的空氣補進來，帶走更多的熱。

throttle.en: Too hot! The chip slows itself down so that it makes less heat. This is called thermal throttling, and it protects the chip from damage.
throttle.zh: 太熱了！晶片自己放慢速度，好讓發的熱少一點。這叫做過熱降頻，是為了保護晶片不被燒壞。

legend.en: Chip color: blue is cool, red is hot
legend.zh: 晶片的顏色：藍色是涼，紅色是燙

legend.en: Orange dots: heat leaving the chip
legend.zh: 橘色小點：離開晶片的熱

legend.en: Gray fins: the heat sink
legend.zh: 灰色鰭片：散熱片

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not a real chip. The temperatures, the 95°C limit, the three workloads, and the three cooling strengths are example numbers chosen to show the idea; real chips have their own limits, which the maker lists in the datasheet. Heat is invisible, so the orange dots are only a picture of it, and the model runs faster than real time.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型，不是真的晶片。溫度、95°C 的上限、三種工作量和三種散熱能力，都是為了說明道理而選的示例數字；真的晶片各有自己的上限，由製造商寫在規格書裡。熱是看不見的，橘色小點只是把它畫出來；模型的時間也比真實的快。

paras: Play a game on a phone for a while, and the back of the phone grows warm. Open many programs on a laptop, and a fan inside begins to spin loudly. Nothing is burning, and nothing is broken. The heat comes from the chip, and making heat is a normal part of a chip's work.

Remember that a chip is made of transistors, which are tiny switches. Each time a switch turns on or off, a little electric charge has to move, and moving it takes a little energy. That energy does not disappear. It turns into heat. One switch makes almost no heat at all, but a chip has billions of switches, and they can switch billions of times every second.

So the harder a chip works, the hotter it gets. When your phone is only showing the clock, few transistors are switching, and the chip stays cool. When you play a game, the chip must draw a new picture many times a second. Many more transistors switch, the chip uses more power, and it makes more heat.

The heat has to go somewhere. In a computer, a piece of metal called a heat sink sits on top of the chip. It has many thin fins, so it has a very large surface that touches the air. Heat moves from the chip into the metal and from the metal into the air. A fan then blows the warm air away so that cooler air can take its place.

A phone has no room for a fan, so it spreads the heat through its body and lets it leave from the surface. That is why you feel the warmth in your hand. If a chip still gets too hot, it protects itself: it slows down so that it makes less heat. You may notice a game becoming less smooth. If slowing down is not enough, the device shuts itself off.

Engineers work hard to make chips that waste less energy. The best trick is lowering the voltage, because a small drop in voltage saves a lot of power. Chips also rest whenever they can, which makes a battery last longer. For the biggest computers, air is not enough, and some are cooled with liquid instead. A cooler chip is a faster and longer-lasting chip.
paras_zh: 用手機玩一陣子遊戲，手機背面就會變熱。在筆電上開很多程式，裡面的風扇就開始大聲地轉。沒有東西燒起來，也沒有東西壞掉。熱是從晶片來的，而發熱本來就是晶片工作的一部分。
還記得嗎？晶片是電晶體做成的，電晶體就是很小很小的開關。開關每開一次或關一次，都要搬動一點點電荷，而搬動它要花一點點能量。這些能量不會消失，它變成了熱。一個開關發的熱少到幾乎沒有，可是一顆晶片有幾十億個開關，每秒還可以開關幾十億次。
所以晶片越忙，就越熱。手機只顯示時鐘的時候，沒有多少電晶體在開關，晶片是涼的。玩遊戲的時候，晶片每秒要畫出好多張新的畫面，開關的電晶體多了很多，晶片用的電變多，發的熱也變多。
熱一定要有地方去。在電腦裡，晶片上面壓著一塊叫做散熱片的金屬。它有很多薄薄的鰭片，所以有很大的表面可以碰到空氣。熱從晶片傳到金屬，再從金屬傳到空氣。接著風扇把熱空氣吹走，讓比較涼的空氣補進來。
手機裡放不下風扇，所以它把熱分散到整個機身，再從表面散出去，你的手才會感覺到溫溫的。如果晶片還是太熱，它會保護自己：放慢速度，讓發的熱少一點。這時候你可能會發現遊戲變得不太順。要是放慢了還不夠，裝置就會自己關機。
工程師很努力地讓晶片少浪費一點能量。最有效的辦法是降低電壓，因為電壓只要降一點點，就能省下很多電。晶片也會一有空就休息，電池因此可以用得更久。對最大的電腦來說，光靠空氣還不夠，有些會改用液體來冷卻。晶片涼一點，就跑得更快，也用得更久。

parts.text_zh: 沒有多少電晶體在開關，發的熱很少。什麼都不裝，晶片也是涼的。

parts.text_en: Better, but in this model the fins alone cannot quite keep up with a game.

parts.text_en: Now the warm air is blown away. The chip runs the game at full speed.

vf.eyebrow: Voltage and Speed · 電壓與速度
vf.en: Why a little less voltage saves a lot
vf.zh: 為什麼電壓降一點點，就省很多
vf.lead_en: The power a chip spends on switching depends on its voltage and on how many times it switches each second. Voltage counts twice: the power goes with voltage times voltage. Move the sliders and see.
vf.lead_zh: 晶片花在開關上的功率，要看電壓，也要看每秒開關幾次。其中電壓要算兩次：功率跟「電壓乘以電壓」成正比。拉拉滑桿看看。
vf.note_en: This follows the rule for switching power: power = C × V² × f, where V is the voltage and f is how often the transistors switch. The three settings are examples, not real products. A real chip also loses some power through small leakage currents, which this calculator leaves out.
vf.note_zh: 這是依照開關功率的公式：功率＝C × V² × f，V 是電壓，f 是電晶體每秒開關的次數。三個設定只是例子，不是真的產品。真的晶片還會因為微小的漏電流多耗一些電，這個計算沒有算進去。

facts.eyebrow: Chip Heat by the Numbers · 晶片發熱的數字
facts.lead_en: Some come from the rule for switching power, and some from the history of computers.
facts.lead_zh: 有些來自開關功率的公式，有些來自電腦的歷史。

items.en: Switching power goes with voltage times voltage. Twice the voltage would mean four times the power.
items.zh: 開關功率跟電壓的平方成正比。電壓變兩倍，功率就變四倍。

items.en: Switching, brief short circuits while a gate changes, and small leakage currents that flow all the time.
items.zh: 開關、邏輯閘切換瞬間短暫的短路，還有一直在流的微小漏電流。

items.en: A paper co-written by Robert Dennard showed that as transistors shrink, the power used by each area of chip can stay the same.
items.zh: 羅伯特．丹納德和同事的論文指出：電晶體縮小時，晶片每單位面積用的電可以維持不變。

items.en: Around this year the old way of scaling ended, because it became too difficult to keep chips cool.
items.zh: 大約在這一年，舊的微縮方式走到盡頭，因為晶片實在太難保持涼爽了。

items.en: The most power used by the Cray-1 supercomputer, designed in 1976. It needed a special cooling system.
items.zh: 1976 年設計的 Cray-1 超級電腦最多用這麼多電，需要特別的冷卻系統。

items.en: Throttling first, then automatic shutdown. Together they protect a processor from overheating.
items.zh: 先降頻，再自動關機。這兩道保護讓處理器不會因為過熱而損壞。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories About Heat · 關於熱的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A rule that worked for thirty years, a wall, a computer in a bath, and the phone in your hand
culture_cards.title_zh: 一條管用三十年的規則、一道牆、泡在液體裡的電腦，還有你手上的手機
culture_cards.lead_en: Heat has shaped how computers are built.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 熱，一直在決定電腦該怎麼做。

cards.body_en: In 1974 Robert Dennard and his coworkers wrote a paper about shrinking transistors. It showed that when transistors get smaller, the voltage and current can shrink too, so each area of the chip uses about the same power as before. Chips could hold more and more transistors without growing hotter.
cards.body_zh: 1974 年，羅伯特．丹納德和同事寫了一篇關於縮小電晶體的論文。它指出：電晶體變小的時候，電壓和電流也可以跟著變小，所以晶片上同樣大小的面積，用的電和以前差不多。晶片可以裝進越來越多電晶體，卻不會越來越燙。

cards.body_en: The rule stopped working around 2005. Chips had become too difficult to keep cool, and engineers call this the power wall. Clock speeds could no longer climb quickly. Most makers turned to another idea instead: putting several processor cores on one chip.
cards.body_zh: 這條規則大約在 2005 年不再管用。晶片變得太難保持涼爽，工程師把這件事叫做「功耗牆」。時脈速度再也沒辦法快速往上衝，大部分的製造商於是改走另一條路：在一顆晶片裡放進好幾個處理器核心。

cards.body_en: The Cray-2 supercomputer was so hard to cool that its designer filled the whole machine with a liquid called Fluorinert. The liquid does not disturb electronic parts. It soaked up the heat and was then pumped out to be cooled with chilled water.
cards.body_zh: Cray-2 超級電腦實在太難冷卻，設計者乾脆把整部機器灌滿一種叫 Fluorinert 的液體。這種液體不會干擾電子零件。它把熱吸走，再被抽到機器外面，用冰水降溫。

cards.body_en: In phones and tablets the parts are packed tightly together, with little or no active cooling, and your hand adds warmth too. So phones often manage their temperature by throttling: the chip slows down for a while until it cools.
cards.body_zh: 手機和平板裡的零件擠得很緊，幾乎沒有主動的散熱裝置，你的手還會再加上一點溫度。所以手機常常用降頻來控制溫度：晶片先慢下來一陣子，等涼了再說。

myths.myth_en: If my phone feels warm, something is broken.
myths.myth_zh: 手機摸起來熱熱的，就是壞掉了。
myths.fact_en: All chips make heat when they work. Warmth during a game or a video call is normal.
myths.fact_zh: 所有的晶片工作時都會發熱。玩遊戲或視訊時溫溫的，是正常的。

myths.myth_en: A fan makes cold air.
myths.myth_zh: 風扇會製造冷空氣。
myths.fact_en: A fan only moves air. It cools a chip by carrying the warm air away.
myths.fact_zh: 風扇只是讓空氣流動。它靠把熱空氣帶走來幫晶片降溫。

myths.myth_en: When a hot phone becomes slow, the chip is wearing out.
myths.myth_zh: 手機變燙之後變慢，是晶片快壞了。
myths.fact_en: The chip is slowing down on purpose to make less heat. When it cools, it speeds up again.
myths.fact_zh: 那是晶片故意放慢，好讓發的熱少一點。涼下來之後，它又會快起來。

myths.myth_en: Smaller transistors always mean a cooler chip.
myths.myth_zh: 電晶體越小，晶片一定越涼。
myths.fact_en: For many years shrinking did keep power in check, but around 2005 chips became too hard to keep cool. Heat is now one of a designer's main worries.
myths.fact_zh: 有很多年，縮小確實讓耗電受到控制；可是大約在 2005 年，晶片變得太難保持涼爽。現在，熱是設計者最傷腦筋的問題之一。

tricks.title_en: Every switch makes a little heat
tricks.title_zh: 每一次開關，都有一點點熱
tricks.body_en: Billions of switches, billions of times a second.
tricks.body_zh: 幾十億個開關，每秒幾十億次。

tricks.body_en: A game heats a chip far more than a clock does.
tricks.body_zh: 玩遊戲比顯示時鐘熱得多。

tricks.title_en: Fins spread it, fans move it
tricks.title_zh: 鰭片把熱攤開，風扇把熱帶走
tricks.body_en: A big surface, then moving air.
tricks.body_zh: 先要有大的表面，再要有流動的空氣。

tricks.body_en: The chip protects itself by doing less.
tricks.body_zh: 晶片用「少做一點」來保護自己。

safety.en: Never open a phone, a computer, or a charger to look at the chip. Parts inside can hurt you, and batteries can be dangerous if they are damaged.
safety.zh: 不要為了看晶片而拆開手機、電腦或充電器。裡面的零件可能會傷到你，電池受損也很危險。

safety.en: Do not cover a laptop's air vents with a blanket or a pillow, and do not leave a phone in a hot car or under a pillow while it charges.
safety.zh: 不要用棉被或枕頭蓋住筆電的出風口；手機充電時不要放在很熱的車裡或枕頭底下。

safety.en: If a device becomes too hot to hold, or its battery looks swollen, stop using it and tell an adult.
safety.zh: 如果裝置燙到拿不住，或是電池看起來鼓起來了，就不要再用，並且告訴大人。

activities.title_en: Warm or Cool? A Phone Survey
activities.title_zh: 溫的還是涼的？手機小調查

materials.en: A phone or tablet that an adult lets you use
materials.zh: 大人同意你用的手機或平板

materials.en: A timer, paper, and a pencil
materials.zh: 計時器、紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Leave the device alone for ten minutes. Touch the back and write down how it feels: cool, a little warm, or warm.
steps.zh: 先把裝置放著十分鐘不要用。摸摸背面，寫下感覺：涼的、有一點溫，還是溫的。

steps.en: Play a video for five minutes. Touch the back again and write down what you feel.
steps.zh: 播五分鐘影片。再摸一次背面，寫下感覺。

steps.en: Play a game for five minutes, if an adult agrees. Touch the back once more.
steps.zh: 如果大人同意，玩五分鐘遊戲。再摸一次背面。

steps.en: Find the warmest spot. The chip is probably near it. Which activity made the most heat, and why?
steps.zh: 找找看哪裡最熱，晶片大概就在那附近。哪一種活動發的熱最多？為什麼？

activities.tip_en: Use only your hand, and stop if the device feels hot. This is a test of warm and cool, not of how hot it can get.
activities.tip_zh: 只用手摸；如果裝置變得很燙就停下來。這是比較溫和涼的實驗，不是要看它能多燙。

materials.en: Two equal sheets of aluminum foil
materials.zh: 兩張一樣大的鋁箔紙

materials.en: Two equal cups of warm water from the faucet (not hot), and a thermometer if you have one
materials.zh: 兩杯一樣多的溫自來水（不要用熱水），有溫度計更好

steps.en: Fold one sheet of foil into a small, tight square. Fold the other back and forth like a paper fan, so that it has many fins.
steps.zh: 把一張鋁箔摺成又小又緊的方塊。另一張像摺扇子一樣來回摺，讓它有很多鰭片。

steps.en: Stand one piece in each cup so that part is in the water and part is in the air.
steps.zh: 兩個杯子各放一塊，讓一部分泡在水裡、一部分露在空氣中。

steps.en: After ten minutes, compare the water in the two cups with the thermometer or with a clean finger.
steps.zh: 十分鐘後，用溫度計或乾淨的手指比較兩杯水。

steps.en: Now blow gently across the fins for a minute, or use a hand fan. Talk about it: which part of the model is the foil, and which part is your breath?
steps.zh: 再對著鰭片輕輕吹一分鐘，或用扇子搧。討論：鋁箔是模型裡的哪個部分？你吹的氣又是哪個部分？

activities.tip_en: The difference may be small. That is an honest result too. Real heat sinks are thick metal pressed tightly against the chip, with paste filling the tiny air gaps between them.
activities.tip_zh: 差別可能很小，這也是誠實的實驗結果。真正的散熱片是厚厚的金屬，緊緊壓在晶片上，中間還塗了散熱膏，把微小的空氣縫隙填滿。

sources.en: Processors consume electrical energy and dissipate it as heat; switching power P = C·V²·f; the three sources of power use (dynamic, short-circuit, leakage); processors are protected by throttling and automatic shutdown
sources.zh: 處理器消耗電能並以熱的形式散出；開關功率 P = C·V²·f；三種耗電來源（動態、短路、漏電）；處理器靠降頻與自動關機保護

sources.en: A heat sink is designed to maximize its surface area in contact with the air; generally, the more surface area, the better it performs; usually made of aluminum or copper; thermal paste fills the air gaps
sources.zh: 散熱片的設計是讓接觸空氣的表面積最大；一般來說表面積越大效果越好；通常用鋁或銅製作；散熱膏填滿空氣縫隙

sources.en: The main role of thermal paste is to eliminate air gaps, which act as thermal insulation
sources.zh: 散熱膏的主要功能是消除空氣縫隙（空氣是隔熱的）

sources.en: Fans reduce temperature by exhausting hot air; all modern processors reduce their voltage or clock speed above a set temperature (thermal throttling); throttling is common in smartphones and tablets, which have little or no active cooling; the Cray-1 (designed 1976) consumed up to 115 kilowatts; the Cray-2 was filled with Fluorinert, which was pumped out to a chilled-water heat exchanger
sources.zh: 風扇靠排出熱空氣降溫；現代處理器超過設定溫度就會降低電壓或時脈（過熱降頻）；手機與平板幾乎沒有主動散熱，常用降頻；Cray-1（1976 年設計）最高耗電 115 千瓦；Cray-2 整機灌滿 Fluorinert，再抽到冰水熱交換器

sources.en: Dennard scaling: as transistors get smaller, their power density stays constant; based on a 1974 paper co-authored by Robert H. Dennard; the regime ended around 2005 at the “power wall,” when it was too difficult to keep the chip cool; most makers turned to multicore processors
sources.zh: 丹納德微縮：電晶體變小時功率密度不變；出自 1974 年羅伯特．丹納德合著的論文；約 2005 年在「功耗牆」結束，因為晶片太難保持涼爽；多數製造商轉向多核心處理器

sources.en: Dynamic frequency scaling adjusts a processor's speed to conserve power and reduce heat, and helps preserve the battery on mobile devices
sources.zh: 動態頻率調整會改變處理器的速度來省電、減少發熱，並延長行動裝置的電池續航

sources.en: The maximum junction temperature of a part is specified in its datasheet
sources.zh: 元件的最高接面溫度寫在它的規格書裡

lessons.title: How Is an AI Chip Different from a CPU?
lessons.title_zh: AI 晶片和一般 CPU 有什麼不同？
lessons.blurb_en: A CPU has a few powerful cores that do one thing after another. An AI chip has hundreds or thousands of small units that all work at the same time. In a 3D model, give both chips the same two jobs and see which one wins each time. Then find out why more workers do not always make a job faster.
lessons.blurb_zh: CPU 有少數幾個很厲害的核心，一件事做完再做下一件。AI 晶片有幾百、幾千個小小的運算單元，全部同時工作。在 3D 模型裡，把同樣的兩種工作交給這兩種晶片，看看每一次是誰贏。再想想看：為什麼幫手變多，工作不一定變快？
lessons.big_idea_en: A CPU is like a few expert workers who can do any job, one step after another. An AI chip, such as a GPU, is like a huge crowd of simple workers who all do the same small job at the same time. AI needs an enormous number of simple calculations that do not depend on each other, so the crowd finishes far sooner. But for a job that must go step by step, the experts are still faster.
lessons.big_idea_zh: CPU 像少數幾位什麼都會的高手，一步接一步地做。AI 晶片（例如 GPU）像一大群只會簡單工作的幫手，大家同時做一樣的小事。AI 需要數量驚人的簡單計算，而且這些計算互不相干，所以一大群幫手快得多。可是遇到一定要一步一步來的工作，還是高手比較快。

lab.title_zh: 四位高手，還是一大群幫手？
lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose a chip: a CPU with 4 big cores, or a GPU with 576 small units. Then choose a job. “Paint a picture” has 576 tiles, and each tile can be done on its own. “A chain of steps” has 48 steps, and each step must wait for the one before it. Watch the board fill up and compare the times.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。先選晶片：有 4 個大核心的 CPU，或是有 576 個小單元的 GPU。再選工作。「畫一張圖」有 576 格，每一格都可以自己做自己的。「一串步驟」有 48 步，每一步都要等上一步做完。看板子怎麼被填滿，比一比花了多少時間。

cpu-paint.en: Each core is fast, but there are only four of them. They go through the tiles one by one, and the picture appears slowly from four places.
cpu-paint.zh: 每個核心都很快，可是只有四個。它們一格一格地做，圖從四個地方慢慢出現。

gpu-paint.en: Each small unit is slow, but there are 576 of them, one for every tile. They all work at the same time, and the whole picture appears almost at once.
gpu-paint.zh: 每個小單元都很慢，可是有 576 個，剛好一格一個。它們同時工作，整張圖幾乎一下子就出現了。

cpu-chain.en: Each step needs the answer from the step before, so only one core can work. But that core is fast, and the chain is soon finished.
cpu-chain.zh: 每一步都要用到上一步的答案，所以只有一個核心能做。不過這個核心很快，一串步驟很快就做完。

gpu-chain.en: Only one small unit can work at a time, and the other 575 must wait. A crowd is no help when the job cannot be shared.
gpu-chain.zh: 一次只有一個小單元能做，其他 575 個只能等。工作不能分的時候，人再多也幫不上忙。

legend.en: Blue blocks: the CPU's 4 big cores
legend.zh: 藍色方塊：CPU 的 4 個大核心

legend.en: Orange grid: the GPU's 576 small units
legend.zh: 橘色格子：GPU 的 576 個小單元

legend.en: Board: dark is waiting, yellow is being worked on, colored is done
legend.zh: 板子：深色還沒做、黃色正在做、有顏色是做完了

lab.scale_en: A teaching model with example numbers. Here a CPU core finishes 12 tiles a second and a GPU unit finishes 1; these speeds, the 4 cores, and the 576 units were chosen to make the idea easy to see. Real chips differ in many more ways, and real CPUs and GPUs work together: the CPU runs the program and hands the big shared jobs to the GPU.
lab.scale_zh: 這是用示例數字做的教學模型。這裡的 CPU 核心每秒做 12 格，GPU 的小單元每秒做 1 格；這些速度、4 個核心和 576 個單元，都是為了讓道理容易看懂而選的。真的晶片還有很多不同的地方，而且真的 CPU 和 GPU 是一起合作的：CPU 負責執行程式，再把可以分工的大工作交給 GPU。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow Wikipedia, “Graphics processing unit” and the other sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依維基百科「Graphics processing unit」條目與本頁最下方列出的其他出處。

paras: Every computer and phone has a CPU, which is its main processor. A CPU follows a program one instruction at a time: it fetches an instruction, works out what it means, and carries it out. It does this billions of times a second. A CPU can do almost any kind of job, and modern ones have several cores, so they can do a few things at once.

In the 1990s, video games gave computers a new kind of job. A picture on a screen is made of a huge number of pixels, and the color of every pixel must be calculated again and again. Each calculation is simple, and most of them do not depend on each other. So engineers built a different kind of chip for this work: the graphics processing unit, or GPU.

A GPU does not have a few big cores. It has hundreds or thousands of small calculation units, and they all work at the same time. Think of painting a long wall. One expert painter is fast, but a thousand children, each with one small square to paint, will finish first. Doing many things at the same time is called working in parallel.

Then scientists noticed something. AI programs called neural networks need the same kind of work: an enormous number of simple multiplications and additions. In 2012 a team in Toronto trained a neural network called AlexNet on two GPUs made for games. It won a famous contest for recognizing pictures, far ahead of the others. After that, GPUs became widely used for AI.

Today some chips are designed only for AI. They are called AI accelerators or neural processing units, and many phones have one inside. But a crowd of small units is not always better. Some jobs must be done in order, because each step needs the answer from the step before. For those jobs, a fast CPU core still wins.

So a computer that runs AI uses both kinds of chips. The CPU is the manager: it runs the program and decides what to do next. The GPU or AI chip is the crowd: it takes the big jobs that can be shared and finishes them quickly. Neither one is simply better. They are good at different things, and they work as a team.
paras_zh: 每一部電腦和手機裡都有 CPU，也就是它的主要處理器。CPU 照著程式，一次執行一個指令：把指令拿出來、弄懂它的意思、然後照著做，每秒可以做幾十億次。CPU 幾乎什麼工作都能做；現在的 CPU 有好幾個核心，所以可以同時做幾件事。
1990 年代，電玩遊戲給了電腦一種新的工作。螢幕上的畫面是由非常多的像素組成的，每一個像素的顏色都要一算再算。每一次計算都很簡單，而且大部分互不相干。於是工程師為這種工作做出另一種晶片：圖形處理器，也就是 GPU。
GPU 沒有少數幾個大核心，而是有幾百、幾千個小小的運算單元，全部同時工作。想像要粉刷一面很長的牆：一位專業油漆師傅動作很快，可是一千個小朋友每人只刷一小格，會先刷完。同一時間做很多件事，叫做「平行」運算。
後來科學家發現了一件事：叫做「神經網路」的 AI 程式，需要的正是同一種工作——數量驚人的簡單乘法和加法。2012 年，多倫多的一個團隊用兩張原本做來玩遊戲的 GPU，訓練出一個叫 AlexNet 的神經網路。它在一場有名的圖片辨識比賽中奪冠，遠遠領先其他隊伍。從那以後，GPU 就被廣泛用在 AI 上。
現在有些晶片是專門為 AI 設計的，叫做 AI 加速器或神經處理器（NPU），很多手機裡就有一顆。不過，一大群小單元不一定比較好。有些工作一定要照順序做，因為每一步都要用到上一步的答案。遇到這種工作，還是速度快的 CPU 核心贏。
所以跑 AI 的電腦兩種晶片都用。CPU 是經理：它執行程式，決定接下來要做什麼。GPU 或 AI 晶片是那一大群幫手：把可以分工的大工作接過去，很快做完。沒有誰一定比較好。它們各有擅長的事，而且是一個團隊。

answers: It follows a program one instruction at a time, very quickly. It has a few powerful cores and can do almost any kind of job.
For graphics. A picture has a huge number of pixels, and each one needs a simple calculation that can be done separately.
AI needs an enormous number of simple calculations that can be done at the same time, which suits a GPU's many small units. But some jobs must be done in order, and then only one unit can work.

amd.eyebrow: More Workers, More Speed? · 幫手越多就越快嗎？
amd.en: The part that cannot be shared
amd.lead_en: Most jobs are a mix: one part can be shared among many workers, and one part must be done by a single worker, step by step. In 1967 the computer scientist Gene Amdahl showed that the part that cannot be shared sets a limit on the speed of the whole job. Move the sliders and look for the limit.
amd.lead_zh: 大部分的工作是混合的：一部分可以分給很多幫手，一部分只能由一個人一步一步做。1967 年，電腦科學家吉恩．阿姆達爾指出：不能分工的那一部分，決定了整件工作最快能有多快。拉拉滑桿，找找看極限在哪裡。
amd.note_en: This is Amdahl's law: speed = 1 ÷ ((1 − p) + p ÷ n), where p is the part that can be shared and n is the number of workers. If half the work can be shared, the job can never be more than 2 times faster. If 95% can be shared, the limit is 20 times.
amd.note_zh: 這是阿姆達爾定律：倍數＝1 ÷（(1 − p) + p ÷ n），p 是可以分工的比例，n 是幫手的數目。如果一半的工作可以分工，整件事最多只能快 2 倍；如果 95% 可以分工，極限是 20 倍。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories About AI Chips · AI 晶片的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A chip made for games, a contest in 2012, a law from 1967, and the chip in your pocket
culture_cards.title_zh: 為遊戲做的晶片、2012 年的比賽、1967 年的定律，還有口袋裡的晶片
culture_cards.lead_en: How a chip for drawing pictures became a chip for AI.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 一顆用來畫畫面的晶片，怎麼變成 AI 的晶片。

cards.body_en: A GPU is a chip designed to process images and speed up computer graphics. In 1999 Nvidia released the GeForce 256 and sold it as “the world's first GPU.” Its job was to draw game pictures quickly. Nobody was thinking about AI.
cards.body_zh: GPU 是為了處理影像、加快電腦繪圖而設計的晶片。1999 年，輝達推出 GeForce 256，用「全世界第一顆 GPU」來宣傳。它的工作是把遊戲畫面畫得又快又好，那時候沒有人想到 AI。

cards.body_en: In 2012 Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and their teacher Geoffrey Hinton at the University of Toronto built a neural network called AlexNet. They trained it on 1.2 million pictures using two GTX 580 graphics cards, and it took five to six days. It won that year's contest by a wide margin.
cards.body_zh: 2012 年，多倫多大學的 Alex Krizhevsky、Ilya Sutskever 和他們的老師 Geoffrey Hinton 做出一個叫 AlexNet 的神經網路。他們用兩張 GTX 580 顯示卡、120 萬張圖片來訓練它，花了五到六天。它以很大的差距贏得那一年的比賽。

cards.body_en: Long before GPUs, Gene Amdahl presented an idea at a computer conference in 1967. However many processors you add, the part of a job that cannot be shared limits the speed of the whole job. It is still used today to predict how much faster a job will run on many processors.
cards.body_zh: 早在 GPU 出現之前，吉恩．阿姆達爾就在 1967 年的一場電腦研討會上提出一個想法：不管加多少個處理器，工作裡不能分工的那一部分，都會限制整件工作的速度。今天，人們還在用它預測一件工作放到很多處理器上能快多少。

cards.zh: 專門為 AI 做的晶片
cards.body_en: Some chips are now designed only for AI. They are called neural processing units (NPUs) or AI accelerators. Google began using its own, the Tensor Processing Unit, in 2015. AI accelerators are also built into the chips of many phones, where they can do AI work quickly or with less power.
cards.body_zh: 現在有些晶片是專門為 AI 設計的，叫做神經處理器（NPU）或 AI 加速器。Google 從 2015 年開始使用自己設計的 TPU。很多手機的晶片裡也有 AI 加速器，讓 AI 的工作做得更快，或是更省電。

myths.myth_en: An AI chip is just a faster CPU.
myths.myth_zh: AI 晶片就是比較快的 CPU。
myths.fact_en: It is built differently: a great many small units that work at the same time, instead of a few powerful cores.
myths.fact_zh: 它的做法不一樣：是非常多個同時工作的小單元，而不是少數幾個很強的核心。

myths.myth_en: A GPU is better than a CPU at everything.
myths.myth_zh: GPU 做什麼都比 CPU 厲害。
myths.fact_en: Only at jobs that can be shared. For steps that must be done in order, a fast CPU core wins.
myths.fact_zh: 只有在可以分工的工作上才是。遇到一定要照順序做的步驟，速度快的 CPU 核心比較快。

myths.myth_en: An AI chip thinks the way a brain does.
myths.myth_zh: AI 晶片像大腦一樣在思考。
myths.fact_en: It does arithmetic: an enormous number of simple additions and multiplications, very fast.
myths.fact_zh: 它做的是算術：數量驚人的簡單加法和乘法，而且做得非常快。

myths.myth_en: Only giant computer centers have AI chips.
myths.myth_zh: 只有巨大的電腦機房才有 AI 晶片。
myths.fact_en: AI accelerators are also built into the chips of many phones.
myths.fact_zh: 很多手機的晶片裡也有 AI 加速器。

tricks.body_en: Any job, one step after another.
tricks.body_zh: 什麼都會，一步接一步。

tricks.body_en: One simple job, everybody at the same time.
tricks.body_zh: 一種簡單的工作，大家同時做。

tricks.body_en: If yes, the crowd wins. If no, the expert wins.
tricks.body_zh: 可以，人多的贏；不行，高手贏。

tricks.body_en: The CPU manages. The GPU does the heavy shared work.
tricks.body_zh: CPU 當經理，GPU 做可以分工的粗重工作。

safety.en: In the classroom activities, walk, do not run, and keep scissors on the table.
safety.zh: 做課堂活動的時候用走的、不要跑，剪刀放在桌上。

safety.en: Never open a computer or a phone to look for the chips inside.
safety.zh: 不要為了找裡面的晶片而拆開電腦或手機。

safety.en: AI tools can be wrong. Check what they tell you, and ask an adult before you share personal information with one.
safety.zh: AI 工具會出錯。它說的話要查證；要把個人資料告訴它之前，先問過大人。

materials.en: A grid of 30 squares drawn on the board, each with a simple sum such as 7 + 5
materials.zh: 黑板上畫 30 格，每格寫一題簡單的加法，例如 7 + 5

materials.en: The same 30 sums on small cards, one for each student, and a timer
materials.zh: 同樣的 30 題寫在小卡上，每人一張；還要一個計時器

steps.en: Round 1: the fastest student in the class solves all 30 sums alone, one after another. Time it.
steps.zh: 第一回合：全班算得最快的同學一個人把 30 題一題一題算完。計時。

steps.en: Round 2: every student gets one card and solves it at the same moment. Time it.
steps.zh: 第二回合：每位同學拿一張卡，同一時間開始算。計時。

steps.en: Round 3: a chain. Start with 1. Each student in turn doubles the number the last student said. Time 10 steps.
steps.zh: 第三回合：一串步驟。從 1 開始，每位同學輪流把上一位說的數字乘以 2。計時 10 步。

steps.en: Talk about it: in which rounds did having more students help? In Round 3, why could only one person work at a time?
steps.zh: 討論：哪幾個回合人多有幫助？第三回合為什麼一次只能一個人做？

activities.tip_en: Round 1 is the CPU, Round 2 is the GPU, and Round 3 is the job that cannot be shared.
activities.tip_zh: 第一回合是 CPU，第二回合是 GPU，第三回合是不能分工的工作。

materials.en: Squared paper cut into strips, one strip for each student
materials.zh: 方格紙剪成一條一條，每人一條

materials.en: Colored pencils, and a rule on the board such as “color a square if its number can be divided by 3”
materials.zh: 色鉛筆；黑板上寫一條規則，例如「號碼可以被 3 整除的格子塗顏色」

steps.en: Number the squares on every strip so that the whole class together covers 1 to 300.
steps.zh: 把每條方格紙編上號碼，讓全班合起來剛好是 1 到 300。

steps.en: Everyone colors their own strip by the rule at the same time. Nobody needs to ask anyone else.
steps.zh: 大家同時照規則塗自己那一條，誰都不需要問別人。

steps.en: Tape the strips together in order and look at the pattern you made.
steps.zh: 把紙條照順序貼起來，看看大家一起做出的圖案。

steps.en: Talk about it: how long would one student need for all 300 squares? Why could this job be shared so easily?
steps.zh: 討論：如果一個人塗 300 格要多久？這件工作為什麼這麼容易分工？

activities.tip_en: Each square depends only on its own number. That is exactly why pixels suit a GPU.
activities.tip_zh: 每一格只跟自己的號碼有關。這正是像素適合交給 GPU 的原因。

sources.en: A GPU is designed for digital image processing and to accelerate computer graphics; modern GPUs include hundreds or thousands of calculation units; their parallel structure led to their adoption in AI

sources.en: Amdahl's law, named after Gene Amdahl and presented in 1967; if 50% of the work can be parallelized the best possible speedup is 2 times, and if 95% can be, 20 times

lessons.title: Why Does a Fab Need So Much Water and Power?
lessons.title_zh: 晶圓廠為什麼需要那麼多水和電？
lessons.blurb_en: The lines on a chip are far smaller than a speck of dust, so a chip factory must be cleaner than any place you have ever been. Staying that clean takes water and electricity. In a 3D factory, follow the water from the city pipe to the wafer and back again, then find the three biggest users of power.
lessons.blurb_zh: 晶片上的線路比一粒灰塵小得多，所以晶圓廠必須比你去過的任何地方都乾淨。要維持這麼乾淨，就要用水、用電。在 3D 工廠裡，跟著水從自來水管流到晶圓、再流回來；然後找出三個最會用電的地方。
lessons.big_idea_en: A chip factory, or fab, uses water and power for one main reason: cleanliness. Wafers are rinsed again and again with ultrapure water, which is much cleaner than drinking water. Fans push filtered air through the cleanroom without stopping, and the machines themselves need a lot of electricity. Because water is precious, fabs clean their used water and use it again.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 晶圓廠用水、用電，最主要的原因只有一個：乾淨。晶圓要用超純水一遍又一遍地沖洗，這種水比飲用水乾淨得多。風扇不停地把過濾過的空氣送進無塵室，機台本身也要用很多電。因為水很珍貴，晶圓廠會把用過的水處理乾淨，再用一次。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. In “Water,” follow the drops: city water is made ultrapure, rinses the wafer, and flows to a reclaim tank. Move the slider to change how much is recycled, and watch the fresh water coming in. Then choose “Power” and press the three buttons to see where the electricity goes.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。在「水」的視角，跟著水滴走：自來水變成超純水、沖洗晶圓，再流到回收水槽。拉動滑桿改變回收的比例，看看進來的新水怎麼變。接著選「電」，按三個按鈕，看電用到哪裡去了。

water.en: Light blue drops are ultrapure water on the way to the wafer. Gray drops are used water. Green drops are cleaned water going back to be used again. The more you recycle, the less city water comes in.
water.zh: 淺藍色的水滴是要送去沖晶圓的超純水，灰色是用過的水，綠色是處理乾淨、要回去再用一次的水。回收得越多，進來的自來水就越少。

air.en: Fans in the ceiling push air down through very fine filters, and the air leaves through the floor. This never stops, so any particle is swept away before it can land on a wafer.
air.zh: 天花板上的風扇把空氣往下吹，穿過很細的濾網，再從地板離開。這件事從不停止，所以微粒還來不及落在晶圓上，就被帶走了。

cool.en: The temperature and humidity of the cleanroom are tightly controlled. Equipment on the roof draws in outside air, cleans it, and cools it before it goes inside.
cool.zh: 無塵室的溫度和濕度都管得很嚴。屋頂上的設備把外面的空氣吸進來，先過濾、冷卻，再送進去。

tools.en: The machines need power too. One EUV lithography machine was measured using 1.31 megawatts, about ten times as much as the older kind of machine.
tools.zh: 機台本身也要用電。一部 EUV 曝光機量到的耗電是 1.31 百萬瓦（MW），大約是舊型機台的十倍。

legend.zh: 水滴：超純水（淺藍）、回收水（綠）、用過的水（灰）

legend.en: Blue boxes in the ceiling: fans with filters
